source.snippet: ServerFault question (Nov 2026): 'We're looking into deploying a self-hosted video conferencing server on our internal network, but we also need external customers to join meetings through a browser without installing a VPN client. The main challenge is keeping the server and internal network protected while allowing guests to connect using a meeting link. I'm considering a setup with a reverse proxy, firewall rules, and a public domain name, but I'm not sure how to handle WebRTC traffic and NAT traversal correctly.'

problem_statement: IT teams at companies wanting self-hosted video conferencing struggle to securely expose meetings to external guests without requiring VPN, with WebRTC NAT traversal and firewall configuration being a recurring technical barrier.
target_segment: IT administrators and infrastructure engineers at privacy-sensitive or compliance-driven SMBs (legal, healthcare, finance) self-hosting collaboration tools.
notes: Business context clear — company deploying for internal + external customer meetings. Organizations in regulated industries pay for self-hosted solutions precisely to avoid cloud vendors. Opportunity: managed TURN/STUN relay service or a configuration-as-a-service product for self-hosted video stacks. Single signal; moderate confidence.
